title: Jensen Huang exits as Nvidia CEO and chip money rotates to Nvidia's rivals and suppliers
intro: Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's departure on Nov 12 after reports tied him to a suspected Chinese intelligence figure, sending Nvidia down about 9% for the week while Congress signaled tighter China export curbs. Money rotated into AMD, Broadcom, memory makers and Japanese and Taiwanese equipment and packaging names, backed by record Applied Materials results and a CoreWeave beat, leaving the tracked total roughly flat from Monday and up 2.6% on the week.
movers_note: Against the Nov 9 close the tracked total slipped 0.20% to $28.21T (about $50B of that is ASML and ASE market caps restated on the source), with Alchip (+29.3%), SUMCO (+18.0%), Powertech (+12.5%), Disco (+11.9%) and Tokyo Electron (+11.4%) leading and Nebius (−18.2%), Nvidia (−8.8%), Quanta Computer (−6.7%), Super Micro (−6.0%) and Cadence (−4.0%) lagging; versus the Nov 6 close the total is up 2.55%.

items.headline: Jensen Huang steps down as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
items.summary: Nvidia's board accepted Huang's exit after reports linked him to a Megaspeed executive whom U.S. intelligence reportedly suspects of spying for China. Kress becomes interim CEO while staying CFO, Harvey Jones becomes board chair, and a search for a permanent CEO has begun. The stock fell more than 13% at the open before closing down 4.3%, and Nvidia still plans to report fiscal Q3 results on Nov 17.

items.headline: Investors rotate out of Nvidia into AMD, Broadcom and TSMC
items.summary: CNBC reports chip investors moved money from Nvidia into AMD, Broadcom and TSMC during the week, citing lower management risk at the rivals and an expectation that Huang's exit loosens Nvidia's hold on the market. SemiAnalysis' Dylan Patel said Huang's supplier ties helped Nvidia lock up scarce capacity, and that Google and Amazon could gain ground without him.

items.headline: Congress leans toward tighter China chip-export curbs after the Nvidia scandal
items.summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune said new China chip-export restrictions are highly likely, with the Chip Security Act, MATCH Act and AI Overwatch Act all candidates to ride on the defense authorization bill, though no deal exists yet. Semafor reports Nvidia sold $4B of chips to Megaspeed, which the Justice Department is investigating over suspected diversion to China.

items.headline: Applied Materials posts a record $10.41B quarter and guides above $11B
items.summary: Fiscal Q4 revenue rose 53% from a year earlier to a record $10.41B, with non-GAAP EPS of $4.16 and full-year revenue of $34.45B. The company guided fiscal Q1 2027 revenue to $11.10B plus or minus $0.5B and said its Semiconductor Systems business is on track to grow more than 40% in calendar 2026 on AI demand.

items.headline: CoreWeave beats and raises as its backlog reaches $132.5B
items.summary: Q3 revenue grew 168% to $3.66B and backlog rose to $132.5B from $104B in June. CoreWeave lifted 2026 revenue guidance to $13B–$13.3B, set 2026 capex at $37B–$39B, and said it does not expect recent data-center ballot measures to affect it.

items.headline: Nebius lifts 2026 capex to $27B and plans $40B–$45B for 2027; shares slide
items.summary: Q3 revenue jumped 571% to $980.8M, ahead of estimates, but Nebius steered 2026 revenue toward the low end of its $3B–$3.4B range. It raised 2026 capex to $27B from $20B–$25B and guided 2027 capex to $40B–$45B against $12B–$13B of 2027 revenue, after raising $5.75B of debt in the quarter; the stock fell about 16%.

items.headline: Analysis suggests export-banned Blackwell chips trained leading Chinese AI models
items.summary: Researcher Will DePue's study of model weights points to Moonshot's Kimi K3 and DeepSeek's V4 having been trained on Nvidia Blackwell chips barred from China. TechCrunch cites Epoch AI's estimate that about 2 million advanced chips reached China in 2024 and 2025 through concealment, while cautioning the chips may have sat in offshore data centers such as Malaysia.
